title: Open-model trust badges and buyer's guide
content:
Purpose:
Provide a lightweight, buyer-friendly framework for positioning open models in the Redwood model catalog. The idea: instead of only technical spec sheets, offer simple trust signals (badges + short narrative) and a buyer's guide that maps common product use-cases to recommended model tiers.

TL;DR (for sales and marketing):
- Introduce three concise trust badges for open models: "Usage-proven", "Latency-optimized", "Quality-validated".
- Pair each badge with a 1-line claim + 1-sentence evidence statement (e.g., "Quality-validated — MBR >= 0.86 on Redwood dialogue evals; tests & prompts available").
- Publish a short buyers' guide that maps 5 buyer personas to model choices and expected tradeoffs (cost / latency / quality).

Why this helps (problem we solve):
- Customers get overwhelmed by raw model metrics and architecture names; they want signals about whether a model is production-ready for their use-case.
- Sales and AE teams need repeatable language to reduce discovery time and quickly establish trust.
- Marketing needs bite-sized creative assets for landing pages and datasheets.

Badge definitions and acceptance criteria (proposal):
1) Usage-proven
   - Claim: "Used in production-scale workloads / stable release"
   - Evidence: >= 3 independent internal or external deployments, documented incident rate < 1% for inference errors in last 90 days, example customer/benchmark links.
2) Latency-optimized
   - Claim: "Optimized for <X ms 99th pct latency on our Dedicated config"
   - Evidence: standardized latency benchmark run on Redwood Dedicated profile (include sequence lengths), quantization/compilation config in public doc.
3) Quality-validated
   - Claim: "Meets Redwood evaluation thresholds for the target task class"
   - Evidence: evaluation artifacts (prompt suites, reference sets, MBR or BLEU-like scores) and a short human review summary.

Additional optional micro-badges: "Safety-scrubbed", "Privacy-locked (KMS)" for models with additional verification steps.

Buyer personas and one-line guidance (examples):
- Indie dev / prototyper: prioritize cost and availability. Recommended: lightweight Usage-proven model variant; callout: "fast spin-up + low per-token cost".
- Product PM (consumer-facing chat): prioritize quality and latency. Recommended: Quality-validated + Latency-optimized combo.
- Data platform / embeddings use-case: prioritize embedding stability & throughput. Recommended: Usage-proven embedding model with index-level guidance.
- Platform / internal tools team: prioritize predictable SLA and isolation. Recommended: Dedicated offering + models with Usage-proven + Privacy-locked.
- Regulated enterprise (legal/finance): prioritize auditability. Recommended: Private deployment + Safety-scrubbed & Quality-validated models; provide eval artifacts and config manifests.

Model selection taxonomy (simple matrix to include in the buyer's guide):
- Axes: (Cost intensity: low -> high) vs (Quality sensitivity: low -> high).
- Map example model families to quadrants with a 1-line rationale. This is a living doc; keep it lightweight so AEs can memorize.

Competitive notes (short):
- Cloud AI marketplaces: emphasize breadth + host-managed infra. Our angle: we combine infrastructure flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private) with baked-in inference economics guidance and verified artifacts.
- LLM API providers: strong on SLAs and simplicity; our edge: transparent performance profiles and open-model verification gives customers migration/pathway to lower cost when appropriate.
- Inference runtimes / self-hosted vendors: they sell control; we sell control plus curated, production-ready model experience and rollout tooling.

Core messaging pillars to test (headline language examples):
- "Pick with confidence: model badges that explain when a model is ready for production."
- "From prototyping to SLA-backed deployments — the catalog that tells you what will work for your workload."
- "Transparent performance and quality artifacts for open models — no guesswork."

Objections and rebuttals (AE crib notes):
- Objection: "Open models are risky / immature."
  - Rebuttal: "We surface standardized verification evidence — tests, benchmarks, and example deployments — so you can evaluate the exact risks. Plus fallback policies and dedicated configs reduce blast radius."
- Objection: "How do I know the model will scale?"
  - Rebuttal: "Each Latency-optimized badge links to a reproducible benchmark and the Dedicated config that matched it; our runtime supports autoscaling and burst policies you can test in staging."
- Objection: "Will quality drift over time?"
  - Rebuttal: "Quality-validated models include prompt/eval suites and a recommended regression monitoring plan (we can onboard the checks into your CI)."

Assets to produce (MKT + sales enablement):
- Short one-page buyer's guide PDF (1–2 pages) with persona map and badge legend.
- Badge assets (SVGs) + alt text and required evidence fields for each badge in the CMS.
- AE cheat-sheet (single-slide) with 3 canned intros and 3 rebuttals.
- Catalog UI metadata schema: minimal required fields for a badge to display (evidence links, last-evaluated date, owner contact).

Rollout plan (quarterly):
- Week 1–4: Finalize badge criteria and create templates for evidence capture.
- Week 5–8: Run verification for top 12 open models in the catalog (triage models for quick wins).
- Week 9–12: Publish buyer's guide + badges; enable AEs with a quick training session and the cheat-sheet.
- Ongoing: Biweekly backlog of candidate models, monthly badge re-evaluation cycle.

Success metrics (what to track):
- Time-to-decision in sales cycle (target: -20% within 3 months).
- Catalog CTR on model cards that include badges (target +30% vs baseline).
- Number of models with full badge evidence captured (target: 70% of top 30 models).
- AE reported confidence (survey) and # of deals citing the guide as helpful.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should badges be binary (present/absent) or graded (bronze/silver/gold)? Recommendation: start binary to reduce overhead; consider tiers after we have coverage.
- Who owns evidence collection? Product-ops + Solutions Eng? Recommend Solutions Eng for first-run onboarding and Product-ops for ongoing maintenance.
- Do we automate badge revocation on failing tests? Ops risk: yes if we limit to non-customer-facing flags initially; need playbook.

Next steps (immediate):
- Kick off a 2-week verification sprint for 6 models (Ben + Omar).
- Design & copy: request 3 badge SVG directions from design (Marta).
- Create a small Confluence template for evidence capture and link it in the catalog entry UI (CON-2318).

Notes / references:
- Link to sample evaluation artifact: CON-2318 (manual), example benchmarks in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-evals.
- Related tickets: JIRA-998-model-catalog-badges (implementation), JIRA-1002-catalog-ui-badges (frontend).

This is a working draft — rough language is intentional so AEs can adapt. Feedback welcome; prefer short, actionable edits rather than long rewrites.
